_note: BIOLOGY ONLY. Compiled from general spearfishing-guide sources (not a validated regional survey), for Southern California's temperate kelp-forest fauna. Depth, temperature, substrate and season of presence and how each species responds to water clarity. None of it is law - California has its own detailed size/bag/season rules (CDFW) that are not encoded anywhere in this app yet.

species.note: The classic SoCal reef fish - resident on rocky reef and kelp holdfasts year round. An important urchin predator; kelp forest health depends on healthy sheephead numbers, worth being selective with big males.
Calico bass - the bread-and-butter SoCal reef and kelp resident, ambushes from cover, holds tight to structure year round.
A flatfish, not a reef fish - it wants open sand near a reef edge rather than the reef itself, so it will score against this app's structure model very differently to the other species here.
Prefers cooler water than the other species on this list and holds deep in rock crevices - more common from Point Conception north but present in deeper, cooler SoCal structure too.
Cautious and mobile along kelp edges rather than resident in one spot - a spring-through-fall species here, thinner on the ground in winter.
A warm-season visitor that patrols structure edges and kelp paddies rather than holding in one spot - relief matters far less to it than current and bait movement, which this app does not model.

_legal_note: Legal rules live in legal/<JURISDICTION>.json and are merged in at run time. No legal pack exists yet for US-CA, so this app will correctly show 'not researched' rather than any size or season claim - California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) publishes the real rules, including species with no-take status.
